Name: selective_self_reference_judge
Title: Selective Self-Reference for LLM-as-a-Judge: Using Self-Consistency to Gate Error Propagation
Short Hypothesis: In solve-then-judge prompting for objective multiple-choice judging, selectively enabling self-reference only on high-agreement (unanimous) self-solves improves judge accuracy compared to always using self-reference (which propagates wrong self-answers), while keeping the benefits of self-reference on high-confidence cases.
Related Work: Lin et al. (2025) 'Do Before You Judge' shows self-reference-guided evaluation improves pointwise correctness judging but warns about error propagation when self-answer is wrong. Xiong et al. (2026) 'PhyCritic' trains a multimodal solve-then-judge critic. Kadavath et al. (2022) and Wang et al. (2022) establish self-consistency as a confidence proxy. Tian et al. (2025) study overconfidence in LLM-as-a-Judge. No prior work gates self-reference in judge prompts using self-consistency as a confidence signal.

notes: Simple algorithm: self-solve k times, check unanimity, gate prompt
Existing results: +6.86pp over no-reference, +0.72pp over always-reference
Error propagation clearly demonstrated: -13.25pp when incorrect consensus
Extend to test with Gemini and additional benchmarks
